state: We no longer have a fixed five-owner limit. The human says the standard library probably dominates and authorizes extra parallel worktree lanes; there are no measurements establishing that size. CanLang presently has a Rust command skeleton, syntax-only editor integration, 39 source examples and 21 desired JS examples. It targets AI-written SaaS with a TS-authored library and direct JS on workerd, canonical authorization/invocation, daisyUI/HTMX and MCP. The human, not Codex, starts every Muse coordinator. Each coordinator uses one checkout and internal agents with disjoint paths, and iterates small commits, own PR review, relevant checks and merges. Existing runtime APIs, Cloudflare resources and suitable packages should be reused. Required semantics include precise values, one commit implementation, current access grants, delivery and file provenance, and actual inline-example execution. D1 optimistic transactional batches and each DO local transaction must not be represented as a distributed transaction. Unsettled history, whole-population and AI forms need a decided specification. We want comparably useful substantial workloads, clear file/interface ownership, early end-to-end execution and controlled disk/CPU use; no timing data predicts scaling. Choice A separates seven owners: unified Rust language+authoring tools; pure standard values/schema/wire codecs; protected state/queries/CRUD/permissions/transactions/migrations/replay; durable execution combined with integrations/files; server UI/localization; identity/HTTP/MCP; and environment assembly/dev/build/deploy/BDD/integration/release work. It reduces handoffs around external effects while leaving asynchronous engine and adapter scope in one lane. Choice B preserves these responsibilities but splits that asynchronous/integration lane into two, for eight owners overall: one handles events/schedules/outbox/receipt behavior, another handles providers and file storage/finalization. It grants provider work its own parallel owner with the cost of more contracts, one more worktree/build footprint and coordination; neither side can ignore agreed dispatch/receipt semantics. Under both choices all queries obtain kernel authority, forms use shared rendering and operations, identity mutations enter kernel commits, shared build/contract files have one owner, and minimal typed producer interfaces precede integrated milestones. Local doubles and syntax checks are limited evidence, not working-app completion.

partition.instructions: Choose the preferable initial lane count and boundary for this same complete scope; weigh the added parallelism against dependency and machine costs.

criteria.A: A: Keep seven lanes and retain one combined asynchronous-services-files owner.
criteria.B: B: Use eight lanes by giving service/file integrations their own owner alongside durable work.
